title: Review: the past tense
why: Review of the "Past Tense" unit: regular verbs, verbs with the vowel a, "to be" and "to have" in the past, and time words, all brought together in a travel story. You finish the first unit of level A2 by telling about a trip from start to finish.

The same markers everywhere: ־תִּי for I, ־נוּ for we, ־תֶּם / ־תֶּן for you (plural), וּ for they. I and we don't change for gender; you (singular and plural) does.

Two more verbs for traveling. טָס (to fly) follows גָּר: טַסְתִּי [tasti], טַסְנוּ [tasnu], הֵם טָסוּ [tasu]. שָׂחָה (to swim) follows הָיָה: שָׂחִיתִי [sakhiti], שָׂחִינוּ [sakhinu].

Telling about a trip

A short story that brings the whole unit together: time words, verbs in the past, \"to be\" and \"to have.\"

בַּקַּיִץ שֶׁעָבַר נָסַעְנוּ לַצָּפוֹן.Last summer, we went up north. [ba-kayits she-avar nasanu la-tsafon]

מַיִם (water) is plural in Hebrew: הַמַּיִם הָיוּ חַמִּים, with the verb and the adjective in the plural.

", "

Traps to avoid

  • \"A year ago\": לִפְנֵי שָׁנָה, placed first; never יֵשׁ.
  • \"Last week\": בַּשָּׁבוּעַ שֶׁעָבַר; \"last year\": בַּשָּׁנָה שֶׁעָבְרָה (agreeing with the noun).
  • \"I was\": הָיִיתִי, for a man and a woman alike; never אֲנִי הָיָה.
  • \"I had a car\": הָיְתָה לִי מְכוֹנִית; the verb agrees with the thing owned.
  • הִיא בָּאָה, הוּא גָּר: written the same in the past and the present; look at the time words.
  • On foot, הָלַכְתִּי; by bus, train, or car, נָסַעְתִּי.

When telling a story, alternate actions (נָסַעְנוּ, אָכַלְנוּ) and descriptions (הָיָה יָפֶה, הָיוּ הַרְבֵּה אֲנָשִׁים), and link them with קֹדֶם, אַחַר כָּךְ, וְאָז, בַּסּוֹף.
